content.comment_body: Hello, I downloaded the [product_name] [version_no] software upgrade for OS X and I'm running Big Sur. After unzipping, I receive a Setup.app file, but when I try to open it, I get a message saying I lack the required privileges to execute it. I'm logged in as the administrator, and previous versions like [product_name] [version_no] and other related tools are installed and working fine. Any suggestions? Thank you, [user_name]
Hi [user_name], please keep in mind that [company_name] has not tested this software with all versions of Mac OS. Please review the attached information.
Understood. Big Sur has been available for a while, so this is a noticeable disadvantage for Apple users. Thank you for the quick support.
Is [company_name] planning a [product_name] [version_no] update to resolve the MacOS Big Sur compatibility issue? Is there an estimated release date for this?
You should direct this question to [company_name] support rather than the forum, as this is a space for user discussion. Please initiate a support request for official information.

I'm not a Mac user, but I've noticed several posts indicating trouble when downloading a [product_name] software upgrade on a Mac. A suggested workaround is to download the upgrade using a Windows PC, then copy it over to the Mac and proceed with installation. From what I recall, the issue may be related to the installer used in [product_name]. The installer is shared across Windows, Mac, and Linux, and often lags behind the latest Mac and Linux OS versions, which leads to installation problems when a new OS is released. Hope this helps.
This solution was very effective! I downloaded and unzipped on Windows, then copied to OS X Big Sur, and the installation worked smoothly. Thank you.
Could you explain how you managed to run a Windows executable on a Mac?

Hello, I'm new to the forum and also a Mac user experiencing the same issue. I have a question: did you download the installation file for Mac or for Windows when using the Windows PC? On my 2011 MacBook Pro with macOS 10.13, I had [product_name] [version_no] operating without issues. Recently, I installed [product_name] [version_no], which also worked fine until my MacBook failed. Now, I'm using an iMac 2011 with macOS 10.13, but I can't upgrade from my DVD-installed [product_name] [version_no] to [product_name] [version_no]. The installer keeps saying it can't locate the correct files from the previous installation, even when specifying the right folder. Although the installation can continue, the newly installed version does not open. Since multiple users seem to face this on Mac, this workaround might benefit many people.

To summarize: use a Windows PC to download the Mac version of the installer, then extract and transfer it to your Mac for installation. The reason appears to be that files downloaded and installed directly on Mac may not work, though the cause is unclear. Perhaps a Mac expert could clarify further.

Hi everyone, this approach did not work for me. I tried various methods and different unzip programs, but wasn't successful. When unzipped on a Windows machine, the Setup.app crashed within seconds. The crash report included details like process identifiers, OS version, memory specs, and exception type, ultimately ending with a termination due to an uncaught exception—launch path not accessible. If anyone has suggestions or technical expertise on resolving this, it would be appreciated.
A new question from [user_name] has been moved to its own thread regarding [product_name] [version_no] download online. Best regards, [user_name] (Moderator)

analysis.insight_summary: Users are experiencing significant installation issues with [product_name] [version_no] on macOS Big Sur. Downloading and unzipping the installer directly on a Mac results in permission errors, even with administrator access. The issue is likely related to how the cross-platform installer is packaged, with a common workaround being to download and extract on Windows before transferring to Mac, which often resolves installation problems. [company_name] has not yet officially tested or updated this software for Big Sur, leading to frustration among Mac users.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect [product_name] upgrades to be directly downloadable, extractable, and installable on macOS Big Sur without the need for a Windows PC or complicated procedures.
